messages:
ana: CI for quickstart started failing after SDK bump, getting 401s on embeddings but curl to REST works. repo: github.com/redwood/sample-apps/llm-quickstart

mike: is it auth header or token format? paste logs?

ana: log:
ERROR: 401 Unauthorized - missing Authorization header
(at node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.js:45)

jordan: sdk v0.12.3 changed header mapping: passing `apiKey` now emits `X-Redwood-Key` for private deployments. looks like hosted expects `Authorization: Bearer`.

sara: that would explain curl (=bearer) succeeding. also saw sample using `timeout_ms` while REST expects `timeout_seconds` -> unit mismatch.

mike: ok two bugs: header mapping leaked into hosted mode, and timeout param units. quickfix: replace SDK call in sample with direct fetch to hosted using Authorization header. e.g.
```js
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-embed-1', input })
})
```

ana: will patch CI to use that. can SDK short-term accept `REDWOOD_API_KEY` as token?

jordan: recommend using `REDWOOD_TOKEN`. plan: revert header fallback for hosted, normalize timeout names (accept ms & seconds), and honor Retry-After. i'll add unit tests.

integrations-bot: created issue #4521: "SDK: hosted header parity + timeout unit normalization" assigned to @mike

mike: i'll open PR for 0.12.4 today, include header revert and retry-after handling for 429/503.

sara: add changelog note and update quickstart README to show fetch workaround and env rename.

ana: CI quickfix pushed with [quickfix] commit. thanks all.
